newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - JUNE 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - JUNE 25.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--State-run hospitals are facing financial problems again, shortly after a favourable resettlement of their debts. The fifteen largest hospitals are losing between 350-600 million drachmas a month, leading to deficits expected to total 70 billion by the end of the year. Experts say at least 20 smaller hospitals should be turned into clinics.
--Gradual deregulation of controls on private rentals comes to a head on July 1 when the six-year process ends and all rentals are determined on the basis of market conditions.

--Actor Anthony Quinn, who immortalised the role of Zorba the Greek in the eponymous film, arrived in Athens yesterday to take part in celebrations on Crete to commemorate the death ot the great Greek writer Nikos Kazantzakis.

--The Supreme Court ruled yesterday that widowers were entitled to receive the pension benefits accorded to their wives: the ruling is based on the principle of equal treatment of the sexes, since widows receive their spouse's pensions on their death.

--Development Minister Vasso Papandreou found herself amidst the fray yesterday with her comments regarding the need to pick up on a recent recommendation for a one-off charge on company profits to held combat unemployment, which pitted her against National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou and his unequivocal refusal of the proposal. Papandreou next faced criticism from Transport Minister Haris Kastanidis over her comments over the minstry's handling of Olympic Airways, following days of delays and cancellations.
--The new Athens international airport at Spata will go into operation in February 2001.

--The body of a young conscript killed last week under suspicious circumstance will be exhumed for a third autopsy to determine the exact cause of death, according to reports. One of the nine soldiers interrogated on the matter so far is reported to have shed light on the murder of the 20-year-old.
--Some 6,000 contract workers of a total 9,500 in local government will receive permanent positions, according to reports.
--Some 350 young people attending the Youth Parliament yesterday raised their voices against the "extinguishing of their dreams" as the session ended.

--State hospitals are in critical condition, with deficits, industrial action by doctors beginning tomorrow and a strike by pharmacies threatening to put the entire health sector out of action. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
